key_insight: Solaris introduces a multiplayer video world model that simulates consistent, action-conditioned multi-view observations, enabling realistic modeling of multi-agent interactions in environments like Minecraft.
problem_solved: Existing action-conditioned video world models are restricted to single-agent perspectives and cannot capture synchronized multi-agent interactions or consistent multi-view observations needed for realistic simulation and multi-agent reasoning.
method: Build a dedicated multiplayer data system for robust, continuous, automated collection of synchronized multi-player, multi-view video trajectories in Minecraft.
Train an action-conditioned video world model that conditions on multiple agents and views to generate consistent, aligned multi-view observations and simulate interaction dynamics.
impact: Solaris enables richer, more realistic world models that capture multi-agent dynamics and cross-view consistency, benefiting research and applications in multi-agent RL, planning, simulation, and data-efficient policy learning.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: multiplayer data collection pipeline → synchronized dataset → Solaris model → multi-view video generation
Before/After comparison: single-agent world model vs Solaris multi-agent multi-view outputs (side-by-side frames)
Multi-view storyboard: synchronized frames from multiple player cameras across time showing consistent interactions
Bar or line chart: improved metrics (e.g., view-consistency, predictive accuracy) comparing Solaris to single-view baselines
paper_title: Solaris: Building a Multiplayer Video World Model in Minecraft
paper_authors: Georgy Savva, Oscar Michel, Daohan Lu, Suppakit Waiwitlikhit, Timothy Meehan
